title: The Crooked Spire
premise: Silas Voss has hidden her magic for seven years in Greyhollow, a city where the Crooked Spire's wards smother all spellwork. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns the Spire itself is a prison holding an ancient god—and her runaway master, Odile, built it that way using Silas's stolen childhood magic as the lock. Hunted by the Spire's witch-finders and shadowed by a disgraced ward-keeper named Tam, Silas must choose: renew the lock with her own life, or unmake the Spire and face the waking god. She chooses a third path—forging a new covenant with the god using found family as anchor—ending the war before it begins, at the cost of her invisibility forever.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes from a drafty attic full of unreliable maps and one very judgmental cat.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In outlawed-magic Greyhollow, Silas sells luck-knots and fever-charves disguised as folk remedies, keeping her true gift buried. A routine sale to a dying child nearly exposes her when the charm visibly works. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life half-lived, and the first crack in her careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass; every star vanishes at once. Panic floods the city, witch-finders sweep the streets, and Silas feels her sealed magic straining like a caged bird. Emotional beat: dread and exhilaration entwined—the world is ending, and part of her is glad.

chapters.title: The Ward-Keeper's Debt
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Disgraced ward-keeper Tam Ashgrave is blamed for the border failure and goes hunting answers—and finds Silas mid-spell saving refugees. Instead of arresting her, he bargains: her knowledge of old magic for his protection. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people who've both failed their duties.

chapters.title: What Odile Left Behind
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Following her master's trail to a burned waystation, Silas finds Odile's journal revealing the truth: the Crooked Spire is a cage, and its lock was forged from magic stolen from Silas as a child. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing her whole identity—her powerlessness was engineered.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Bell
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Witch-finder Captain Ilsa Renn corners them; Tam takes a bell-curse meant for Silas, which slowly unmakes his memories of everyone he loves. They escape into the undercity with the Spire's hunters close behind. Emotional beat: guilt crystallizing into resolve—Silas will not let another person pay her debts.

chapters.title: Beneath the Crooked Stone
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the Spire's foundations they find the god Vhalor—not a monster but a bound, grieving presence that speaks in Silas's own childhood voice. It shows her the original covenant Odile broke. Emotional beat: terror softening into terrible compassion; the enemy is a prisoner too.

chapters.title: A Family of Strays
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Hiding in the undercity, the fugitives gather allies: charm-sellers, deserters, the child Silas once healed. For one night there is warmth—a shared meal, laughter, Tam remembering Silas even as the curse eats his past. Emotional beat: found family taking root, making what comes next unbearable.

chapters.title: The Price of the Lock
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Odile herself appears, dying, and offers the choice: pour Silas's life into renewing the lock, or free Vhalor and risk war. Silas refuses both and strikes out on her own path, and Odile, finally, asks forgiveness. Emotional beat: the climax of identity—rejecting the roles written for her.

chapters.title: Covenant of Small Names
chapters.summary: Silas's POV (climax). Atop the Spire, with witch-finders storming the stairs and stars still dark, Silas offers Vhalor a new covenant: not one sacrifice, but ten thousand small willing gifts from the city's hidden magicians, anchored by names spoken aloud. The Spire straightens; the stars return. Emotional beat: love against duty fulfilled—duty transformed by choice.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Never Invisible
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Greyhollow reckons with its magic; Silas opens a school in the Spire's shadow, teaching openly. Tam, memory-damaged but choosing to build new memories, stays. Odile's grave sits beneath the straightened stone. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—identity no longer hidden, family chosen and kept.
